theory.intro: **Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)** is the global time standard at the Prime Meridian ($0^{\circ}$), with time zones defined by hourly offsets.
facts: The **time difference** between two zones is found by subtracting their offsets: $\text{Difference} = \text{Offset}_1 - \text{Offset}_2$.
A higher (more positive) UTC offset means a location is **ahead** in time.
Adjust for midnight rollover by subtracting $24\text{ hours}$ for the next day, or adding $24\text{ hours}$ for the previous day.
steps: Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$
Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time
Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time
Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)

foundation.question_text: When it is $1{:}00\text{ pm}$ in Cairo ($\text{UTC}+2$), what is the local time in New York ($\text{UTC}-5$)?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -5 - 2 = -7\text{ hours}$
New York is $7\text{ hours}$ behind Cairo.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$1{:}00\text{ pm} = 13{:}00$
$\text{Time in New York} = 13{:}00 - 7\text{ hours}$
$= 06{:}00$
$= 6{:}00\text{ am}$

foundation.question_text: When it is $3{:}00\text{ pm}$ in London ($\text{UTC}+0$), what is the local time in Cairo ($\text{UTC}+2$)?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = 2 - 0 = 2\text{ hours}$
Cairo is $2\text{ hours}$ ahead of London.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$3{:}00\text{ pm} = 15{:}00$
$\text{Time in Cairo} = 15{:}00 + 2\text{ hours}$
$= 17{:}00$
$= 5{:}00\text{ pm}$

foundation.question_text: When it is $11{:}30\text{ am}$ on Wednesday in Sydney ($\text{UTC}+10$), what is the local day and time in San Francisco ($\text{UTC}-8$)?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -8 - 10 = -18\text{ hours}$
San Francisco is $18\text{ hours}$ behind Sydney.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Time in SF} = 11{:}30 - 18\text{ hours} = -6{:}30$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$-6{:}30 + 24{:}00 = 17{:}30\text{ (previous day)}$
It is $5{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Tuesday in San Francisco.

foundation.question_text: When it is $10{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Monday in Anchorage ($\text{UTC}-9$), what is the local day and time in Tokyo ($\text{UTC}+9$)?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = 9 - (-9) = 18\text{ hours}$
Tokyo is $18\text{ hours}$ ahead of Anchorage.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$10{:}00\text{ pm Monday} = 22{:}00$
$\text{Time in Tokyo} = 22{:}00 + 18\text{ hours} = 40{:}00$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$40{:}00 - 24{:}00 = 16{:}00\text{ (next day)}$
It is $4{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Tuesday in Tokyo.

foundation.question_text:
Cate is working in Seoul ($\text{UTC}+9$) and travels to Chicago ($\text{UTC}-6$).
A $14\text{-hour}$ non-stop flight leaves Seoul at $5{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Thursday.
What is the local day and time in Chicago when the flight arrives?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -6 - 9 = -15\text{ hours}$
Chicago is $15\text{ hours}$ behind Seoul.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$5{:}00\text{ pm Thursday} = 17{:}00$
$\text{Departure time in Chicago} = 17{:}00 - 15\text{ hours} = 02{:}00\text{ Thursday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival time in Chicago} = 02{:}00 + 14\text{ hours} = 16{:}00$
$= 4{:}00\text{ pm on Thursday}$

foundation.question_text:
Loretta boards a plane in Fiji ($\text{UTC}+12$) at $2{:}30\text{ pm}$ on 7 April, flying to Miami ($\text{UTC}-5$).
The flight duration is $16\text{ hours}$.
What is the local date and time in Miami when she arrives?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -5 - 12 = -17\text{ hours}$
Miami is $17\text{ hours}$ behind Fiji.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Miami} = 14{:}30\text{ (7 April)} - 17\text{ hours} = -2{:}30$
$-2{:}30 + 24{:}00 = 21{:}30\text{ on 6 April}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival time} = 21{:}30\text{ (6 April)} + 16\text{ hours} = 37{:}30$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$37{:}30 - 24{:}00 = 13{:}30\text{ on 7 April}$
$= 1{:}30\text{ pm on 7 April}$

foundation.question_text:
A flight leaves Melbourne ($\text{UTC}+10$) at $4{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Thursday, bound for Paris ($\text{UTC}+1$).
The flight duration is $23\text{ hours}$.
On what day and at what local time does the flight arrive in Paris?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = 1 - 10 = -9\text{ hours}$
Paris is $9\text{ hours}$ behind Melbourne.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Paris} = 16{:}00\text{ Thursday} - 9\text{ hours} = 07{:}00\text{ Thursday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival time in Paris} = 07{:}00\text{ Thursday} + 23\text{ hours} = 30{:}00$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$30{:}00 - 24{:}00 = 06{:}00\text{ on Friday}$
$= 6{:}00\text{ am on Friday}$

development.question_text: When it is $9{:}30\text{ am}$ in New York ($\text{UTC}-5$), what is the local time in Chicago ($\text{UTC}-6$)?
development.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -6 - (-5) = -1\text{ hour}$
Chicago is $1\text{ hour}$ behind New York.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Time in Chicago} = 09{:}30 - 1\text{ hour}$
$= 08{:}30$
$= 8{:}30\text{ am}$

development.question_text: When it is $1{:}20\text{ am}$ on Tuesday in Dubai ($\text{UTC}+4$), what is the local day and time in London ($\text{UTC}+0$)?
development.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = 0 - 4 = -4\text{ hours}$
London is $4\text{ hours}$ behind Dubai.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Time in London} = 01{:}20\text{ Tuesday} - 4\text{ hours} = -2{:}40$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$-2{:}40 + 24{:}00 = 21{:}20\text{ (previous day)}$
It is $9{:}20\text{ pm}$ on Monday in London.

development.question_text:
In December, Mr Ding flies from Sydney ($\text{AEDT } \text{UTC}+11$) to Shanghai ($\text{UTC}+8$).
His plane departs Sydney at $9{:}00\text{ am}$ and the flight duration is $10\text{ hours}$.
What is the local time in Shanghai when he arrives?
development.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = 8 - 11 = -3\text{ hours}$
Shanghai is $3\text{ hours}$ behind Sydney.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Shanghai} = 09{:}00 - 3\text{ hours} = 06{:}00$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival in Shanghai} = 06{:}00 + 10\text{ hours} = 16{:}00$
$= 4{:}00\text{ pm}$

development.question_text:
Melbourne is 11 hours ahead of UTC ($\text{UTC}+11$).
Honolulu is 10 hours behind UTC ($\text{UTC}-10$).
A plane departs Melbourne at $7{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Tuesday and lands in Honolulu after a $9\text{-hour}$ flight.
What is the local day and time in Honolulu when the plane lands?
development.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -10 - 11 = -21\text{ hours}$
Honolulu is $21\text{ hours}$ behind Melbourne.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$7{:}00\text{ pm Tuesday} = 19{:}00$
$\text{Departure in Honolulu} = 19{:}00\text{ Tuesday} - 21\text{ hours} = -2{:}00$
$-2{:}00 + 24{:}00 = 22{:}00\text{ on Monday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival in Honolulu} = 22{:}00\text{ (Monday)} + 9\text{ hours} = 31{:}00$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$31{:}00 - 24{:}00 = 07{:}00\text{ on Tuesday}$
$= 7{:}00\text{ am on Tuesday}$

development.question_text:
The time in Brisbane is $4.5\text{ hours}$ ahead of New Delhi.
Harriet flew from New Delhi to Brisbane via Singapore.
Her flight left New Delhi at $11{:}30\text{ am}$ on Monday (New Delhi time), stopped for $3\text{ hours}$ in Singapore, and arrived in Brisbane at $9{:}00\text{ am}$ on Tuesday (Brisbane time).
What was the plane's total flying time?
development.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
Brisbane is $4.5\text{ hours}$ ahead of New Delhi.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Brisbane time} = 11{:}30\text{ am} + 4\text{ h } 30\text{ min} = 16{:}00\text{ on Monday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Total elapsed time} = 16{:}00\text{ Monday to } 09{:}00\text{ Tuesday}$
$= 8\text{ hours (to midnight)} + 9\text{ hours} = 17\text{ hours}$
$\text{Total flying time} = 17\text{ hours} - 3\text{ hours (stopover)}$
$= 14\text{ hours}$

development.question_text:
A direct flight departs City $A(0^{\circ}, 30^{\circ}\text{E})$ at $10{:}00\text{ am}$ on Friday for City $B(0^{\circ}, 120^{\circ}\text{E})$.
The flight duration is $8\text{ hours}$.
Using $15^{\circ} = 1\text{ hour}$ to determine the time difference, what is the local time in City $B$ upon arrival?
development.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 120^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{90^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 6\text{ hours}$
City $B$ is $6\text{ hours}$ ahead of City $A$.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in City } B = 10{:}00 + 6\text{ hours} = 16{:}00$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival time} = 16{:}00 + 8\text{ hours} = 24{:}00$
$= 12{:}00\text{ am (midnight)}$

development.question_text:
A traveler flies from Sydney to San Francisco in May.
Sydney uses standard time ($\text{UTC}+10$), while San Francisco observes daylight saving ($\text{UTC}-7$).
If the flight departs Sydney at $9{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Wednesday and takes $13\text{ hours } 20\text{ minutes}$, what is the local time and day in San Francisco on arrival?
development.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = -7 - 10 = -17\text{ hours}$
San Francisco is $17\text{ hours}$ behind Sydney.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$9{:}30\text{ pm Wednesday} = 21{:}30$
$\text{Departure in SF} = 21{:}30\text{ Wednesday} - 17\text{ hours} = 04{:}30\text{ on Wednesday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival in SF} = 04{:}30\text{ (Wednesday)} + 13\text{ h } 20\text{ min} = 17{:}50$
$= 5{:}50\text{ pm on Wednesday}$

mastery.question_text:
A passenger flies from London ($\text{UTC}+0$) to Sydney ($\text{AEST } \text{UTC}+10$).
The flight leaves London at $8{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Wednesday, has a $4\text{-hour}$ layover in Dubai, and arrives in Sydney at $6{:}00\text{ am}$ on Friday.
Calculate the total flying time (excluding the layover).
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
Sydney is $10\text{ hours}$ ahead of London.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Departure in Sydney time} = 20{:}00\text{ Wednesday} + 10\text{ hours} = 30{:}00 = 06{:}00\text{ on Thursday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Total elapsed time} = 06{:}00\text{ Thursday to } 06{:}00\text{ Friday} = 24\text{ hours}$
$\text{Total flying time} = 24\text{ hours} - 4\text{ hours (layover)}$
$= 20\text{ hours}$

mastery.question_text:
An online international conference links researchers in Linköping $(58^{\circ}\text{N}, 16^{\circ}\text{E})$ and Sydney $(33^{\circ}\text{S}, 151^{\circ}\text{E})$.
If a keynote presentation in Sweden starts at $8{:}00\text{ pm}$ on Thursday Swedish local solar time and runs for $2\text{ hours } 15\text{ minutes}$, what local day and time in Sydney does the presentation conclude? (Apply $15^{\circ} = 1\text{ hour}$; ignore daylight saving).
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 151^{\circ} - 16^{\circ} = 135^{\circ}$
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{135^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 9\text{ hours}$
Sydney is $9\text{ hours}$ ahead of Sweden.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$\text{Keynote start in Sydney} = 20{:}00\text{ Thursday} + 9\text{ hours} = 29{:}00 = 05{:}00\text{ on Friday}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Conclusion time} = 05{:}00 + 2\text{ h } 15\text{ min} = 07{:}15$
$= 7{:}15\text{ am on Friday}$

mastery.question_text:
A return flight leaves San Francisco ($\text{UTC}-7$, daylight saving) at $10{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Friday and flies for $14\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$ to Sydney ($\text{UTC}+10$, standard time).
What is the local day and time in Sydney when the flight arrives?
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the time difference: $\text{Destination UTC offset} - \text{Origin UTC offset}$**
$\text{Difference} = 10 - (-7) = 17\text{ hours}$
Sydney is $17\text{ hours}$ ahead of San Francisco.
2. **Convert the starting time to 24-hour format and adjust by the time difference to find the corresponding destination time**
$10{:}30\text{ pm Friday} = 22{:}30$
$\text{Departure in Sydney time} = 22{:}30\text{ Friday} + 17\text{ hours} = 39{:}30$
$39{:}30 - 24{:}00 = 15{:}30\text{ on Saturday (3:30 pm)}$
3. **Add the journey duration (and any stopover time) to calculate the arrival time**
$\text{Arrival time in Sydney} = 15{:}30\text{ (Saturday)} + 14\text{ h } 40\text{ min} = 30{:}10$
4. **Adjust for midnight rollover (subtract 24 hours for next day, add 24 hours for previous day)**
$30{:}10 - 24{:}00 = 06{:}10\text{ on Sunday}$
$= 6{:}10\text{ am on Sunday}$
